title: How much of 'semantic systems are efficient' is the efficiency of a structural constraint? A weighting-free comparison across colour, indefinites, modals and quantifiers

cost.compute_notes: Reuses the re-implementations in denic2022-*/reanalysis/core.py and imel2026-modal-typology-efficiency/reanalysis/mcore.py, and the saved per-language samples in steinertthrelkeld2021-*/reanalysis/out/out_q2_ladder.json. One script, about two minutes. Colour (x2): the authors' model zip re-fetched (sha256 eb25ae01..., identical to the morning), only pM and pU_M kept (859,940 B npz, sha256 9988f6f6...), zip deleted; 102 languages x 60 convex + 60 random partitions, a few minutes.

claims.statement: [Colour added after the first draft -- see quantities and why.] Measured by net Pareto dominance (P(natural dominates null) - P(null dominates natural), on complexity and informativeness, weighting-free), natural systems overwhelmingly beat random systems of the same size in all three domains (+0.92 indefinites, +0.96 modals, +0.62 quantifiers), and a descriptor-matched structural null removes 84% of that advantage for indefinites, more than all of it for modals, and 41% for quantifiers.
claims.scope: Indefinites: 40 Haspelmath languages vs overlap-free systems with the same size and coverage. Modals: 28 inventories (drop_syn branch) vs distinct IFF systems with the same size, coverage and overlap; Table-5 prior. Quantifiers: no attested inventories; 'natural' = languages drawn from the 101 quasi-natural quantifiers, vs languages of fully monotone and conservative non-natural quantifiers of the same size, complexity NOT matched.

our_assessment.why: This replaces the 'about nine-tenths in every domain' phrasing I used earlier the same day, which compared gap shares built in different geometries (cidral was asked to attack exactly that). In a common, weighting-free metric the pattern is real but uneven. Indefinites: a small positive residual for natural systems remains (CI excludes 0). Modals: natural systems are WORSE than the structural null. Quantifiers: a large residual remains, and it is entirely formula length -- quasi-natural quantifiers are shorter in the LoT, and when complexity is matched the structural null wins on informativeness. Common thread: wherever natural systems retain an edge over the structural null, the edge is on the COMPLEXITY axis, and complexity is measured in a representation language designed by theorists of the same phenomena (Haspelmath's features; the quantifier LoT; the modal LoT whose atoms are the IFF axes). No function-word domain shows an informativeness advantage over the structural null. CORRECTION after adding colour (x2): colour scores +0.17 [0.12, 0.21] vs convex (83% removed, close to indefinites), and its residual is on BOTH axes (0.065 bits simpler, 0.024 bits more accurate), with an information-theoretic complexity rather than a hand-built LoT. So the first draft's 'the edge is always on theory-built complexity, never on informativeness' does not hold for colour. Revised: structure removes 83-84% (colour, indefinites), all (modals), 41% (quantifiers, where the rest is LoT formula length). Instrument check (x3_metric_known_answer.py): a 'natural' point drawn from the null scores ~0 (|mean| <= 0.03 over 9 spread/correlation settings), so the metric is unbiased; it is invariant to monotone rescaling of either axis (rank-based, like an AUC), which is why it is weighting-free; but it is a STANDARDISED effect -- the same raw improvement scores +0.68 against a tight null and +0.20 against a wide one. Hence '% removed by structure' compares positions within two different null distributions: read it ordinally, not as a ratio of effect sizes. Second caveat: matching on descriptors such as overlap conditions on something that is itself a route to efficiency, so 'removed by structure' means 'decomposed into', not 'explained away'. ADDED 19:40: colour's residual is PRIOR-DEPENDENT -- under a uniform source natural mode maps do not beat random convex partitions (-0.048). So in every domain where an edge over the structural null survives, it comes from a quantity built from the same data or theory: colour's LI prior (from naming data), numerals' need (English frequencies), indefinites' features (Haspelmath on the same languages), quantifiers' LoT. None survives a source of that quantity independent of the systems judged.

claims.statement: The 'within the human range' criterion used to call emergent neural colour-naming systems efficient (chaabouni2021) is met by 93.5% of random convex partitions of CIELAB and by 0% of random partitions.
claims.scope: Released IB model (zaslavsky2018), WCS soft encoders as the human range (102 languages), 600 random Voronoi partitions with K drawn from WCS mode-map term counts.

quantities.name: share_random_convex_partitions_with_inef_in_human_range
quantities.baseline: random non-convex partitions 0.0; human Inef range 0.041-0.333

our_assessment.why: Direct computation with the authors' own model; extends the convex null from human languages to emergent communication. The complexity range is not reproduced by the null (convex 1.1-3.7 bits vs human 1.0-2.6), so complexity control remains a genuine, separate signal.

claims.statement: Decomposed along a ladder of null descriptors, the natural advantage is carried almost entirely by two things: the domain's structural universal (modals: restricting the null to IFF meanings takes net dominance from +0.96 to +0.26) and overlap (matching it takes indefinites from +0.94 to +0.48 and IFF-modals from +0.19 to -0.24). Matching size, exact-synonym removal and coverage changes almost nothing (all rungs within 0.04).
claims.scope: Indefinites (40 Haspelmath languages; null items drawn from all 63 flavour sets) and modals (28 inventories; null meanings from all 63 or from the 21 IFF meanings); per-language nulls by rejection sampling (200 matched draws, 60,000 tries); net Pareto dominance with bootstrap CI over languages.

quantities.baseline: all-meanings pool size only +0.964; IFF pool +distinct 0.226, +coverage 0.191, +overlap -0.243 (-0.413 to -0.069)

quantities.name: net_dominance_indefinites_overlap_matched
quantities.baseline: size 0.924, +distinct 0.924, +coverage 0.935; overlap-free partitions with same size and coverage (x1) 0.147

our_assessment.why: Answers part of the 'which descriptors' objection empirically: the choice is not a free parameter in effect, because only two descriptors move the result. It does not answer the conceptual half: overlap (synonymy avoidance) is itself a classic efficiency principle, so whether matching it 'removes' or 'explains' efficiency is a question of framing the data cannot settle. Rejection sampling could match overlap for only 34/40 indefinite and 15/28 modal languages from the unconstrained pool; those rungs describe a selected subset.

open_questions: PRIOR ART (found 16:06, via Chaabouni et al. 2019's citation): Moscoso del Prado Martin (2013), 'The missing baselines in arguments for the optimal efficiency of languages', CogSci 35 (escholarship.org/uc/item/7738n7cz). NOT read in full -- both hosts blocked automated download this session; per its published abstract it argues that linear frequency-length / lexical-measure correlations are what maximum entropy predicts for random systems and computes random-system baselines showing corpus correlations WEAKER than chance. Same principle (efficiency claims need a baseline from a system without the hypothesised pressure), different object (frequency-length correlations, not semantic-category partitions). Any write-up must cite it and claim only the extension: structural (not random) nulls for category-efficiency analyses, the descriptor ladder, and the implementation audits. Read it in full before writing anything.

SELECTION CAVEAT (added 16:00 by the author against herself): the domains were chosen by me after the frame existed, and in modals the null was tightened AFTER the loose null broke the pattern. The descriptor ladder (c3) shows every rung, which limits the damage, but 'six domains agree' (with xu2020 and chaabouni2021) is weaker evidence than it sounds. What would count: a domain chosen by someone else, with the null ladder fixed before computing. Ask cidral or lucas to pick the next domain and the rungs blind.
Add colour: rerun zaslavsky2018 c2 saving IB complexity and accuracy per Voronoi draw (needs the 73 MB model), then compute the same net dominance.
Which descriptors to match is a choice. Report the full ladder (size -> +distinct -> +coverage -> +overlap) per domain and say where the residual crosses zero, rather than one matched null.

Independent complexity measures (vocabulary size, entropy, a learned LoT) would test whether the remaining complexity-axis edge is a property of languages or of the representation language. imel2026 already shows natural modals lose their edge under vocabulary size and entropy.
